leaves.what: The page, the bordered panel at desktop width, each step's heading and form, the signed-in ending, written by hand in src/screens/SignInAndUp.tsx.
Focus is moved by hand to each step's heading (tabIndex -1, a ref, an effect) when the step changes.
leaves.why: The stepper block shows where a person is and does not hold the steps' content, so nothing moves focus or announces the new step.

leaves.what: onStepPress is passed only on the verify step, so only 'Account' is gone back to and only before the email is verified.
leaves.why: The block makes every done step a button or none: it has no way to say which done steps may be returned to. Solved from outside, without editing the block.

parts.notes: Sign up has three steps (Account, Verify email, About you), sign in two (Sign in, Verify). Not seen in a browser: the block's phone form ('2 of 3: Verify email') is taken on its doc comment's word.

parts.part: Email and password with show and hide

leaves.what: Show and hide is a toggle IconButton passed as an element to TextField's trailingIcon, with -mr-2 to sit as Material's trailing icon does, and the input's type switched in a wrapper (PasswordField).
leaves.why: TextField has no password form. Its doc comment says a trailing icon may be 'a clear button' only in passing, in a code comment: that the slot takes a pressable element had to be confirmed in icons.tsx (renderIcon) and field-styles.ts.

leaves.what: Read TextField's body, icons.tsx's renderIcon and field-styles.ts to learn that trailingIcon accepts an interactive element and that no overlay covers it.
leaves.why: The doc comment does not say the slot is interactive, nor what margin a button in it needs.

leaves.what: Validation is a resolver written by hand, since the adapter's Form* fields do not pass `rules` to Controller.
leaves.why: The adapter takes only control and name: a rule per field is not possible, and no schema library is installed.

leaves.what: After a refused submit the first invalid input is found with querySelector('[aria-invalid=true]') and focused by hand.
leaves.why: The adapter does not hand react-hook-form the field's ref, so shouldFocusError has nothing to focus.

leaves.what: Read Button's source to learn what isLoading does: it swaps the icon for a spinner and nothing else.
leaves.why: isLoading has no doc comment. The press is not held and nothing is announced, so a second submit is refused in the handlers.

leaves.what: Passed autoCapitalize to the text field: a type error, removed.
leaves.why: React Aria's TextField does not take it; assumed any input attribute went through.

parts.notes: The toggle keeps the name 'Show password' and changes aria-pressed; its icon swaps between an eye and a struck eye (lucide-react). A trailingIcon replaces the kit's error icon, as its doc says, so an invalid password shows its error by colour and message only. Demo account: maya@example.com / harbour-2026. Not seen in a browser.

leaves.what: TextField, Label, Input, FieldError and Text from react-aria-components, in src/screens/OtpField.tsx.
leaves.why: The kit has no one-time-code field, and its TextField cannot draw the code as cells.

leaves.what: Six cells drawn by hand under one transparent real input (autocomplete one-time-code, numeric keyboard, paste filtered to digits, caret held at the end, a drawn caret, submit when the sixth digit arrives).
leaves.why: No kit component. One input rather than six keeps the keyboard's code suggestion, paste and a single labelled field for a screen reader.

leaves.what: The cells follow the kit's outlined text field by eye: 56dp tall, extra-small corner, outline at rest, 2dp primary on the cell typed, error when refused.
leaves.why: Nothing in the kit or Material to follow for a code field.

leaves.what: `animate-pulse` for the drawn caret, `max-w-12` for a cell: Tailwind's own, not motion or size tokens.
leaves.why: The kit has no caret or blink token.

parts.notes: The code is 482913. A wrong code clears the cells, says so and keeps focus; the field is read-only while the code is checked. Resend is disabled for 30 seconds with a countdown in its label, then sends a snackbar and returns focus to the field. Selecting part of the code is not possible (the caret is held at the end): Backspace removes the last digit. Not seen in a browser: the transparent input's alignment over the cells and iOS's suggestion are untested.

parts.part: Consent checkbox with a link in its label

leaves.what: The error message under the checkbox is a Body written by hand, tied to it with aria-describedby and a role=alert wrapper.
leaves.why: A lone Checkbox takes isInvalid and has no errorMessage; only CheckboxGroup has one, and a group of one is not a consent.

leaves.what: Read Checkbox's source to see how its label lays out children.
leaves.why: The label is an inline-flex row: text with links in it becomes several flex items. The sentence is wrapped in one span and the row set to items-start; the doc comment does not say so.

leaves.what: The links open a small terms or privacy page (src/screens/LegalPage.tsx, `?page=terms`) in a new tab, by a real href.
leaves.why: A Link without href is a span, and a press on it inside a label would also tick the box; a real href inside a label does not. Nothing in the kit says which is safe.

parts.notes: Unsure: React Aria's press handling on the label may show the checkbox's pressed state layer while a link in it is pressed. The checkbox's name read by a screen reader holds both links' text. Not seen in a browser.

leaves.what: Google's mark is an SVG with Google's four hex colours (src/screens/GoogleMark.tsx).
leaves.why: A brand's mark is drawn in its own colours, not a role.

leaves.what: The 'or with your email' line between two Dividers.

parts.notes: 'Continue with Google' simulates the provider's round trip with a timer and signs in as the demo customer. While it loads the mark is replaced by the kit's spinner and the form's submit is disabled. Not seen in a browser.

general_leaves.why: The kit ships no icon set beyond its own few, and says so.

friction: Nothing here was seen running: no browser was allowed, so the screen is verified by tsc, vite build and one server render only. In the kit: (1) nothing says how to make a password field; that TextField's trailingIcon takes a pressable element, and that a 40dp IconButton needs -mr-2 there, was learnt from three source files. A line and an example in TextField's doc comment would do. (2) Button's isLoading has no doc: it does not hold the press nor set aria-busy, which a form's submit needs. (3) The react-hook-form adapter passes neither `rules` nor the field's ref: validation needs a resolver, and focusing the first error is done by hand; the skill's section on the adapter says neither. (4) A lone Checkbox has no errorMessage, and its doc does not say children must be one node for a sentence with a link, nor whether a Link inside the label is safe. (5) No one-time-code field and no block for one: the most hand-written part of the screen. (6) The stepper block has no say on which done steps may be gone back to, and no word on moving focus between steps.
